title: The Iron Road
description: You witness the assassination of a royal courier on the Iron Road. The satchel he carried falls at your feet. The killers turn toward you. You run. What you carry could change the fate of three kingdoms — if you survive long enough to deliver it.

scripts.onLoad: state.set('suspicion', 0); state.set('satchelOpened', false); state.set('borderPassType', 'none'); state.set('courierTokenRevealed', false); state.set('spymasterDebt', 0); state.set('guardCaptainBribed', false); state.set('contactAlive', true); state.set('satchelDestination', 'undelivered')
scripts.onStart: ctx.showMessage('The Iron Road stretches before you — three kingdoms, countless enemies, and a sealed satchel whose contents could end you.')

items.name: Sealed Satchel
items.description: A royal courier's leather satchel, sealed with wax bearing an unfamiliar crest. Something vital is inside. You do not know what.

items.name: Courier's Token
items.description: A bronze disc stamped with the royal courier corps insignia. Marks the bearer as an agent of the Crown — or as a target.

items.name: Forged Border Pass
items.description: A convincing forgery of a merchant's border pass. Close inspection may reveal the deception.

items.name: Legitimate Border Pass
items.description: A genuine border pass issued by a border city official. Purchased at a price, but valid under scrutiny.

items.name: Spymaster's Letter
items.description: A sealed letter from the Spymaster offering safe passage in exchange for the satchel. The seal is intact — for now.

items.name: Bribe Purse
items.description: A purse of mixed coin, assembled for greasing palms and opening doors. Each use depletes it.

items.name: Traveller's Cloak
items.description: A plain, dusty cloak that helps you blend into the road's traffic. Wearing it reduces suspicion at checkpoints.

scripts.onEquip: state.set('cloakWorn', true); ctx.showMessage('Wrapped in the cloak, you look like any other traveller on the road.')

items.name: Healing Potion
items.description: A small vial of red restorative. Restores 4 STAMINA when drunk.

scripts.onUse: ctx.modifyStat('STAMINA', 4); ctx.removeItem('Healing Potion'); ctx.showMessage('Warmth floods through you. Some of your strength returns.')

items.name: Assassin's Blade
items.description: A slim, well-balanced knife taken from one of the killers. A professional's tool. Adds 1 to your SKILL while equipped.

scripts.onEquip: ctx.modifyStat('SKILL', 1); ctx.showMessage('The blade feels balanced in your hand.')

items.name: Spy Ring Cipher
items.description: A folded card of encoded text given by a border spy. Proves connection to the spy ring — and implicates you if found.

scripts.onPickup: state.set('suspicion', state.get('suspicion') + 3); ctx.showMessage('Carrying this makes you a marked person.')

items.name: Noble's Invitation
items.description: A formal invitation to the estate of a minor noble on the second kingdom road. Provides cover for your journey.

items.name: Relay Station Key
items.description: A key to the royal relay station between the second kingdom and the capital. Issued to authorised couriers only.

chapters.title: The Ambush Site
chapters.brief:
NARRATIVE PURPOSE: This chapter launches the adventure. The player witnesses a professional assassination on the Iron Road, finds the courier's satchel at their feet, and is forced to flee into the surrounding forest while the assassins pursue. By the end of the chapter the player has escaped and stands at the edge of the road that leads toward the border city. The chapter must establish the tone — fast, dangerous, morally unresolved — and put the key items (Sealed Satchel, Courier's Token) into play. It sets up but does not resolve the identity of the factions or their motives.

SETTING:
- The Iron Road: the great stone highway running between kingdoms, wide enough for two wagons abreast, heavily trafficked by merchants and soldiers. At the ambush site the road cuts through a dense forest; there are no witnesses.
- The Forest Verge: the mixed woodland immediately off the road. The player flees into this. There are gullies, a dry streambed, and a ruined waystone marker.
- The Waystation: a small, partly collapsed stone shelter a kilometre from the ambush. Travellers use it for rest. Currently unoccupied but may have been searched by the assassins.

NAMED CHARACTERS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- The Courier (dead before section 1 ends): a royal courier of middle years, plainly dressed for discretion, carrying the sealed satchel. The player sees him fall. No dialogue.
- The Lead Assassin: the commander of the kill team. Wears no insignia. Cold, efficient, gives orders in a clipped undertone. Speaks once directly to the player if cornered ("Give us the satchel and walk away."). Does not reveal the lord they serve.
- The Tracker: a second assassin who pursues the player into the forest. Can be evaded, fought, or briefly spoken with under duress.

ITEMS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- Sealed Satchel (KEY): gained at section 1 or early flight. The player's possession of it is the premise of the adventure. Must be carried on exit.
- Courier's Token (KEY): found on the courier's body; the player may or may not take it. Taking it raises suspicion slightly but opens royal-faction dialogue options in later chapters.
- Assassin's Blade (EQUIPPABLE): can be taken from the Tracker if the player defeats or disarms them. Optional.
- Healing Potion (USABLE): found in the Waystation. Optional.
- Traveller's Cloak (EQUIPPABLE): found in the Waystation, left by a previous traveller. Reduces suspicion at checkpoints. Optional.

TONE: Immediate, kinetic, slightly disorienting. The player has no time to plan. Short sections with clear danger. Combat is possible but never forced — evasion should always be an option.

ARC CONTRIBUTION: The chapter answers 'what happened?' and forces the player into possession of the satchel. It raises but does not answer: Who sent the assassins? What is in the satchel? Can you trust anyone? The player should feel exposed and uncertain by the chapter's end.

SECTION RANGE: 1–40. Section 1 is the adventure's start section.

GATE REFERENCES:
- This chapter's entry gate: section 1 (no incoming gate — first chapter).
- Exit gate to ch2: section 41. Exit sections within this chapter that leave for the border city must target section 41.
- The player MUST carry Sealed Satchel on exit. Courier's Token is optional. Any optional items (Assassin's Blade, Healing Potion, Traveller's Cloak) may or may not be carried.

forbidden: Player must not carry 'Forged Border Pass'
Player must not carry 'Legitimate Border Pass'

chapters.title: The Border City
chapters.brief:
NARRATIVE PURPOSE: This chapter is the intrigue hub of the adventure. The player arrives in Varenmark, the frontier border city that straddles the trade route between the first and second kingdoms. Here they must acquire a border pass to cross into the second kingdom, navigate corrupt officialdom, encounter the spy ring and the Spymaster's first contact, and manage rising or falling suspicion. The chapter introduces all three factions explicitly: the assassins' network (operating through street-level agents), the border spy ring (whose members approach the player at the inn), and a first hint of royal intelligence (through the Guard Captain's knowledge of the courier). By the end, the player has a border pass of some kind and has made at least one significant alliance or enmity decision.

SETTING:
- Varenmark: a dusty, densely-packed frontier city. Stone buildings pressed close. A main market square, a customs gatehouse at the far end where the road continues into the second kingdom.
- The Ironbell Inn: the principal travellers' inn near the market. Factions meet here. The Spymaster's first contact operates here.
- The Customs House: where border passes are inspected and issued. The Guard Captain's domain.
- The Back Lanes: the alleys and side streets where the spy ring operates. Shortcuts exist here but also ambushes.
- The Forger's Workshop: hidden, reached through the Back Lanes. Can produce a Forged Border Pass.

NAMED CHARACTERS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- The Spymaster: appears through a proxy at first (a contact at the Ironbell Inn) and, if the player follows the thread, in person in a private meeting room. Offers protection and guidance in exchange for the satchel — or for information about its contents. The Spymaster is not hostile here but the price of their help grows. The player should leave ch2 feeling that the Spymaster knows more than they admit.
- The Border Guard Captain: commands the customs gatehouse. Corrupt but pragmatic. Will accept a bribe to issue a Legitimate Border Pass or to look away at the crossing. Not cruel — he has no strong faction loyalty. Can be an unexpected ally in ch3 via a message he sends ahead, if bribed generously.
- The Spy Ring Contact: approaches the player at the Ironbell Inn. Mid-level operative, nervous, acting on instructions. Offers the Spy Ring Cipher and intel on the assassins in exchange for being told what the satchel contains. Accepting the Spy Ring Cipher raises suspicion (it implicates the bearer) but opens spy ring safe routes in ch3.
- The Forger: a minor character reachable through the Back Lanes. Produces the Forged Border Pass for a fee. No faction loyalty.

ITEMS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- Sealed Satchel (KEY): carried in, must be carried out. Never leave it in this chapter.
- Courier's Token (KEY): if carried in, it is a risk — royal agents in the city may identify the bearer. Can be hidden or discarded.
- Forged Border Pass (KEY): obtained from the Forger. Raises suspicion by 2 when inspected at the crossing. Lowers it if the inspection is bypassed.
- Legitimate Border Pass (KEY): obtained by bribing the Guard Captain. Costs coin or a favour.
- Bribe Purse (USABLE, countable): can be assembled from the player's gold or found at the inn. Useful for the Guard Captain and other encounters.
- Spy Ring Cipher (KEY): offered by the Spy Ring Contact. Carrying it raises suspicion significantly.
- Spymaster's Letter (KEY): given by the Spymaster if the player meets them directly. Provides access to the Spymaster's network in ch3.
- Healing Potion (USABLE): available for purchase at the market.

TONE: Slow-burn, layered. Information is power. The danger here is not combat but exposure. The player should feel watched. Every transaction has a cost beyond coin.

ARC CONTRIBUTION: The chapter answers 'who wants the satchel and why?' — not completely, but enough. The player makes the first significant moral choice: who, if anyone, to contact or trust. By the end the player should know the Spymaster's face, the Guard Captain's price, and at least one fact about the assassination's patron that they did not know before.

SECTION RANGE: 41–90.

GATE REFERENCES:
- Entry gate from ch1: section 41.
- Exit gate to ch3: multiple branches based on border pass type. All exit sections target ch3.
  - If player carries 'Legitimate Border Pass': entry section 91 (smooth crossing).
  - If player carries 'Forged Border Pass': entry section 92 (risky crossing, suspicion check).
  - If player carries neither: entry section 93 (back road crossing, dangerous but low suspicion).
- On exit: Sealed Satchel MUST still be carried. At least one border pass must be carried OR the player has taken the back road (state.backRoadTaken == true).

assumedState: state.satchelOpened is false or true (player may have attempted to open it in ch1)

forbidden: Player must not carry 'Forged Border Pass' (only one pass type carried)
Player must not carry 'Legitimate Border Pass'
Player must not carry 'Legitimate Border Pass'
Player must not carry 'Forged Border Pass'

normalize: Set state.backRoadTaken = true at section 93 onEnter

chapters.title: The Second Kingdom
chapters.brief:
NARRATIVE PURPOSE: This chapter moves the player across the second kingdom — open road, noble estates, and a royal relay station — toward the capital's outer approaches. The journey seems more open than the border city but is not safe: the assassins have agents ahead, the spy ring has a safe house at a noble estate, and the relay station is where royal intelligence first confronts the player directly. The chapter forces the critical trust decision: who do you hand the satchel to, if anyone? It closes with the player entering the capital region. The Courier's Contact is first mentioned as a destination here.

SETTING:
- The Open Road: the Iron Road resumes its width and visibility here. Merchant caravans, noble coaches, and military patrols are regular traffic. Being on the road means being seen.
- The Crossroads Inn: a large roadside inn at the junction to the capital route. Neutral territory — everyone stops here. The assassins' handler has an agent here.
- Goldmere Estate: a minor noble's country estate two hours off the main road. The spy ring maintains a contact here. The Noble's Invitation provides cover for visiting.
- The Relay Station: a fortified waystation operated by the royal courier corps. This is where Courier's Contact may be waiting — or may have already been killed. Royal intelligence is present here.
- The Capital Approach: the road narrows between quarried stone walls as it enters the capital's outer district. This is the chapter exit.

NAMED CHARACTERS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- The Courier's Contact: the intended recipient of the satchel. An elderly official connected to royal intelligence. May be at the Relay Station alive and waiting, dead (if the assassins moved faster), or relocated (if royal intelligence evacuated them). The player's choice of route here affects the Contact's fate.
- The Lord's Agent: the assassins' handler. Appears in person for the first time at the Crossroads Inn, posing as a merchant. Offers to buy the satchel outright. Polished, unhurried, and more dangerous than the killers who work for them. This is not the final chapter encounter — they escape if confronted here.
- The Noble Host: the owner of Goldmere Estate. A minor noble with spy ring sympathies. Provides shelter, the Noble's Invitation as cover, and access to a spy ring courier who can carry a message to the capital ahead of the player.
- The Relay Station Warden: a royal courier corps officer. Suspicious of the player but bound by protocol. May issue the Relay Station Key if the player carries the Courier's Token.

ITEMS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- Sealed Satchel (KEY): carried in, must be carried out unless handed to a faction here (which triggers a branch ending or a chapter 4 variant).
- Border Pass (KEY, either type): no longer needed after the border; may be discarded or used as cover story material.
- Courier's Token (KEY): if carried, the Relay Station Warden recognises it and the royal-faction path opens.
- Spy Ring Cipher (KEY): if carried, the Noble Host recognises it and the spy ring path opens.
- Spymaster's Letter (KEY): if carried, opens an additional route to the Spymaster's capital contact.
- Noble's Invitation (KEY): gained from the Noble Host at Goldmere Estate. Used as cover for road checkpoints.
- Relay Station Key (KEY): gained from the Relay Station Warden if the player qualifies. Opens a shortcut into the capital.
- Healing Potion (USABLE): available at the Crossroads Inn for purchase.

TONE: Deceptively open, then closing. The countryside looks peaceful; the danger is beneath the surface. The Lord's Agent's appearance should feel like a chess player moving a piece into check — no violence yet, just pressure.

ARC CONTRIBUTION: By the end of this chapter, the player has made their trust decision or committed to delivering the satchel personally. They should understand what is likely in the satchel even if they have not opened it. The Lord's Agent's appearance makes the antagonist visible and personal. The chapter leaves the player one step from the capital with alliances or enemies in place.

SECTION RANGE: 91–130.

GATE REFERENCES:
- Entry gates from ch2: sections 91 (legitimate pass), 92 (forged pass — suspicion check on entry), 93 (back road — low suspicion on entry).
- Exit gate to ch4: section 131. All paths through this chapter converge at section 131.
- On exit: Sealed Satchel must be carried unless state.satchelDeliveredEarly == true (rare branch).

assumedState: state.backRoadTaken may be true (if entry via section 93)

normalize: Section 92 onEnter: run a SKILL_TEST; on failure increase state.suspicion by 3 and show message that the forged pass aroused suspicion
Section 93 onEnter: decrease state.suspicion by 1 to reflect the back road's lower profile

possible: Player may carry 'Sealed Satchel' (unless state.satchelDeliveredEarly == true)

chapters.title: The Capital
chapters.brief:
NARRATIVE PURPOSE: The final chapter. The player is in the capital city — crowded, layered, and dangerous. The suspicion score now has teeth: high suspicion means guards check papers, factions have agents at the gates, and the Lord's Agent may strike before the player reaches their destination. The chapter must deliver on the adventure's central promise: the player decides what to do with the satchel. There are at least four endings — deliver it to the Courier's Contact or royal intelligence (if alive), hand it to the Spymaster, sell it to the Lord's Agent, or destroy it — and each has distinct narrative consequences.

SETTING:
- The City Gates: the first checkpoint. High-suspicion players face hard choices here. Low-suspicion players pass more easily.
- The Market District: the commercial heart of the capital. Crowds provide cover. The Spymaster's proxy operates out of a covered market stall.
- The Docks: a secondary approach to the palace district, used by those who want to avoid main roads. The spy ring has a contact here.
- The Palace District: the sealed inner quarter around the royal palace. Only those with the Relay Station Key, the Courier's Token, or a Spymaster's Letter can access it directly.
- The Palace Anteroom: the delivery point for royal intelligence. The Courier's Contact (if alive) waits here or has been replaced by a royal intelligence officer.

NAMED CHARACTERS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- The Courier's Contact: present in the palace anteroom if still alive (state from ch3). If dead, replaced by a royal intelligence officer who is harder to convince but can still receive the satchel.
- The Lord's Agent: appears in person with a final offer — more threatening now. If suspicion is very high, they may attempt to take the satchel by force.
- The Spymaster: present in person at the market district contact point. The price they name here is their final offer. If the player has the Spymaster's Letter, the price is lower.
- The Capital Gate Captain: enforces the city gate checkpoint. Bribable, but the cost scales with suspicion.

ITEMS IN THIS CHAPTER:
- Sealed Satchel (KEY): the central object of all endings. Its fate determines the victory type.
- Courier's Token (KEY): grants access to the palace district and establishes credibility with royal intelligence.
- Relay Station Key (KEY): alternative access route to the palace district.
- Spymaster's Letter (KEY): reduces the Spymaster's price and opens the palace district back route.
- Assassin's Blade (EQUIPPABLE): useful if the Lord's Agent turns hostile.
- Healing Potion (USABLE): last resort before confrontations.

ENDINGS:
- Royal Delivery (VICTORY): deliver the satchel to the Courier's Contact or royal intelligence. Requires access to the palace district. Outcome varies by suspicion level.
- Spymaster's Deal (VICTORY): hand the satchel to the Spymaster. A compromise — you survive, but the message's fate is uncertain.
- Lord's Sale (VICTORY, morally grey): sell the satchel to the Lord's Agent. You walk away wealthy. The message is destroyed.
- Destruction (VICTORY): burn the satchel at the docks before anyone can have it. No one wins. No one dies.
- Death by Exposure (INSTANT_DEATH): high suspicion + wrong choices = caught and executed.

TONE: Taut, converging, consequential. Every section should feel like it matters. The player should feel the weight of all their decisions from the previous chapters. Short, punchy sections near the end.

ARC CONTRIBUTION: Closes all open questions. Reveals what was in the satchel (in the delivery ending). Pays off every faction thread. The player should feel that their choices — every bribe, every trust decision, every suspicion-raising confrontation — directly shaped the outcome.

SECTION RANGE: 131–170.

GATE REFERENCES:
- Entry gate from ch3: section 131.
- No exit gates — this chapter contains all endings.

assumedState: state.suspicion is an integer (0 = unsuspected; 5–9 = known; 10+ = actively hunted)
state.satchelOpened may be true or false
state.contactAlive may be true or false
state.satchelDeliveredEarly is false (if true, player was routed to an early ending in ch3)

sections.narrative:
The Iron Road runs wide and straight through the forest, paved in pale grey stone worn smooth by a thousand years of trade. You are a traveller — unremarkable, unhurried — walking the verge when the carriage ahead of you stops without warning.

There is no drama in what happens next. Four figures step from the treeline. They do not shout. They do not run. They move with the quiet efficiency of men who have done this before. The coachman goes first, a single blow, and then the door swings open and a plainly dressed man of middle years is dragged into the road.

A royal courier. You recognise the cut of his coat even from here.

He struggles. He does not beg. Something falls from his hand — a leather satchel, sealed with dark wax — and skids across the stone toward your feet.

The four figures look up. The nearest one, the commander, meets your eyes. He speaks in a flat voice: "Don't."

You pick up the satchel anyway.

choices.text: Run into the forest — now, before they reach you
Stand your ground and face the commander

sections.narrative:
You hold the satchel and you do not move. It is a foolish choice, or a brave one — you cannot tell from the inside.

The commander walks toward you. He is unhurried. The others fan out to cut off the road in both directions. He stops three paces away and looks you over with the detached interest of a man appraising livestock.

"Give us the satchel," he says, "and walk away. You were never here. You saw nothing. We have no quarrel with travellers."

His voice is almost kind. His eyes are not.

choices.text: Hand over the satchel
Refuse and run for the forest
Ask him who he works for

sections.narrative:
You break left, off the stone road and into the forest verge, crashing through undergrowth with the satchel clutched under your arm. Behind you there is a short pause — the pause of men deciding — and then the sound of boots on earth.

They are fast. Trained. But the forest here is dense and tangled, gullied by old seasonal floods, and you know how to move in rough ground. You duck under a low branch, skid down a shallow bank, and come up running along a dry streambed.

For a moment you cannot hear them behind you. You press deeper into the dark between the trees.

choices.text: Keep running along the streambed
Leave the streambed and climb the gully bank to the north
Hide in the hollow under the bank and wait

sections.narrative:
You set the satchel down on the road between you.

The commander picks it up. He checks the wax seal — intact — and tucks it under his arm. Then he looks back at you, and something changes in his expression: a small, flat appraisal.

"Thank you," he says.

He nods once to the man on his left.

You do not feel the blow. There is only the road rising toward you, and then nothing.

A traveller who knows nothing and can identify no one is still a witness. The Iron Road does not forgive loose ends.

"Who do you work for?" you ask. The words are out before you finish thinking them.

The commander is quiet for a moment. Then he almost smiles — not warmly, but with a certain respect for the question.

"Someone you have never heard of," he says. "Someone who would prefer the contents of that satchel never reach their destination. That is all you need to know, and more than most people learn."

He extends his hand.

"The satchel. Now."

choices.text: Give him the satchel
Run

sections.narrative:
The streambed runs north-east, cutting between stands of beech and old hawthorn. The stones underfoot are smooth and dry, and you move fast, keeping low. Your breath is loud in the silence.

Then you hear it: a single footfall, deliberate, not far behind. Someone is tracking you — staying just close enough to keep contact, not close enough to force a confrontation. A professional.

The streambed curves ahead. To the right, you can see the outline of a ruined waystone marker, half-buried in moss, and beyond it a faint path threading away through the trees.

choices.text: Follow the path beyond the waystone
Keep to the streambed and increase your pace
Stop at the waystone and prepare for the tracker to reach you

sections.narrative:
You scramble up the gully bank on hands and knees, loose earth crumbling under your grip. At the top you are in a stand of old pine, the ground needled and soft, the trees spaced wide. Good ground to move in.

You can hear voices below — two of them, speaking in short, clipped sentences. They have split up. One is following the streambed. The other is ahead of you, cutting around to intercept at the forest edge.

You need to decide quickly.

choices.text: Push through the pine stand to the north — away from both voices
Backtrack along the high bank and try to circle back behind them
Press east toward the forest edge and the open road beyond

sections.narrative:
You press yourself flat under the cut bank, the root-threaded earth inches above your face, the satchel clamped against your chest. You control your breathing.

Boots crunch on the streambed stones. One pair, moving fast, scanning. The tracker passes within four metres. You see boots, trousers tucked into them, a long knife in a plain scabbard. He stops. He listens. A long moment.

Then he moves on.

You give it a count of thirty before you allow yourself to breathe properly.

The path beyond the waystone is old and faint — a deer trail, perhaps, or a charcoal burner's route from another era. It leads uphill through dense hazel coppice. You push through, branches catching at your clothes.

After ten minutes the coppice thins and you find yourself on a low ridge, looking north. Below, barely visible through the canopy, is a pale grey roof and a collapsed wall: a waystation. Stone-built. Solid.

Behind you, nothing. You may have lost them.

choices.text: Descend to the waystation
Wait on the ridge and watch the station before approaching

sections.narrative:
You run. The streambed bends east and you follow it, lungs burning, the satchel jouncing against your side. Stones clatter under your feet, announcing every step.

You can hear them gaining — faster than you on the open ground of the streambed, where there is nothing to break line of sight. This was a mistake.

The streambed narrows ahead. A fallen tree blocks it. You have two options and no time.

choices.text: Vault the fallen tree and keep running
Climb the bank and turn to face whoever is coming

sections.narrative:
You stop. You turn. You put your back to the waystone's bulk and you wait.

The tracker emerges from the shadows between the trees. He is younger than you expected — perhaps thirty, with a weathered face and the economical posture of someone trained to move without wasted motion. He carries a short blade at his side, not yet drawn.

He looks at the satchel. Then at you. He does not seem surprised.

"You can put that down," he says. "Or we can do this the other way."

choices.text: Set down the satchel and talk
Draw whatever you have and fight
Feint left and bolt past him into the trees

sections.narrative:
The pine stand runs for a good half kilometre. You move fast but quietly, weaving between the tall trunks, heading north by the light filtering through the canopy. The voices fade behind you.

You emerge eventually onto a faint cart track, probably used by foresters. It runs east-west. East will take you back toward the Iron Road eventually. West disappears into deeper woodland.

You pause and listen. The forest behind you is quiet. For the first time since the road, you feel something like margin — not safety, but room to think.

choices.text: Follow the cart track east toward the road
Follow it west, deeper into the forest
Leave the track entirely and head north toward higher ground

sections.narrative:
You circle back along the high bank, moving low and careful, angling to put both voices ahead of you. It works — you can hear them below now, quartering the streambed, calling to each other in short syllables that mean nothing to you.

But circling costs time, and time has a price. By the time you reach the stretch of road you escaped from, you can see that the coachman's body has been moved and the coachman's couch is gone. The courier's body is still there. No one on the road; no witnesses.

The satchel's wax seal has grown warm against your palm from being clutched so tightly.

choices.text: Search the courier's body before leaving
Leave immediately — north along the road toward the waystation

sections.narrative:
You move east, toward where the forest thins near the road. Bad choice. The assassin who circled ahead is waiting at the tree line — you almost walk into him.

He spots you at the same moment. He is bigger than the tracker, broader across the shoulders, and he does not hesitate. He charges.

You have no time to run.

The tracker passes and does not double back. After a full minute of silence you ease out from beneath the bank, shaking earth from your hair, and listen.

Nothing. The forest has absorbed them.

You press north, keeping off the streambed this time, moving through the undergrowth where your footsteps make no sound. The forest thickens, then opens, and ahead you see the pale shape of a stone building through the trees.

A waystation. Old, partly collapsed on one side, but the main room is intact.

choices.text: Approach the waystation

sections.narrative:
Your cover holds for twenty minutes. Then the tracker reverses. You hear his boots at the edge of your hearing — a deliberate, careful tread — and then he is above you on the bank, looking down at the hollow where you are pressed.

He drops in beside you before you can move.

"Don't," he says. He is not breathing hard.

He crouches to your level, close. His blade is in his hand but angled away — not a fighting grip, something more ambiguous.

"Listen to me," he says, low and urgent. "He'll tell you to walk away. He won't mean it. I've watched him work. Give me the satchel, now, and I'll tell him you outran us. You'll be alive tonight."

choices.text: Give him the satchel
"What's in it?"
Attack him while he's close

sections.narrative:
You vault the fallen tree and land badly, your ankle twisting on a hidden stone. You keep running, but slower now, limping. Behind you, boots crunching on bark as whoever was following clears the obstacle.

The streambed opens into a small clearing. At the far edge is a crumbling stone wall — the boundary of something, overgrown with bramble. Beyond it: more trees, the slope rising.

You need to choose a direction.

choices.text: Climb over the wall and continue north
Hide in the bramble against the wall

sections.narrative:
You set the satchel on the ground between you. But you do not release it — your hand stays on the strap.

The tracker watches this. He gives a small, flat smile.

"You're not going to give it to me," he says. It is not a question.

He crouches to your level, keeping his hands visible, the blade still sheathed. His eyes move to the satchel, then back to your face.

"Listen carefully," he says quietly. "The man I work for will kill you regardless of what you do with that bag. I've watched him work. You have one option: run north, find the waystation on the hill, wait until dark. Don't go back to the road before then."

He stands. He looks at you for a moment.

"Don't tell him I said that."

choices.text: Take the warning and head north

Close up, the Spymaster looks less like a spy and more like a senior administrator: comfortable weight, good cloth, grey at the temples, eyes that have been recording everything in this room since you walked in. He has drunk half his wine.

"Good," he says, as if you have just answered a question he asked some time ago. "Sit down. I dislike people hovering."

He studies you for a moment.

"You have the satchel. Yes — I can see that. I don't want to take it from you. What I want is considerably more interesting."

choices.text: "Who are you?"
"What do you want?"
Say nothing and listen

sections.narrative:
The door the colour of old blood is in the third alley past the fish stall, exactly as described. You knock twice, pause, then twice more. A bolt draws back.

Inside: a small, windowless workshop lit by three oil lamps. Engraving tools laid in neat rows. A drying rack of pressed sheets. The young man from the market — Kallos, you assume — is seated at the work table and does not look up.

"Merchant's pass. Three gold for standard, four if aged with a use-seal. Show me your face — the name is yours to choose, within reason."

choices.text: Commission the standard Forged Border Pass for three gold
Commission the aged and sealed version for four gold
You cannot afford it — leave

sections.narrative:
The knock pattern works. The door opens. You are looked over by a very large and very quiet man who says nothing, steps back, and lets you in.

The Forger looks up from his work table. He takes you in with the same clinical eye he turns on everything.

"I don't know you," he says. "How did you find this address?"

This is the beginning of a negotiation.

choices.text: "I followed you from the market."
"Someone pointed me this way."

sections.narrative:
You slip through the side door into a corridor that smells of paper and old ink. Clerks move ahead of you, heads down over their work. You are three steps inside before a guard you did not see turns from a wall recess and looks at you.

"Visitors through the main hatch," he says.

He has not drawn his weapon. He has not called for help. He is assessing whether you are someone who made an honest mistake or someone he needs to make a different decision about.

choices.text: "I have an urgent message for the Captain. Personal delivery."
Apologise and back out, return to the main queue

sections.narrative:
The Captain arrives in three minutes. He looks at the Courier's Token on the table, then at you, and then picks it up.

He turns it over in his fingers. The kind of familiarity that means he has seen them before.

"The courier came through my gate six days ago. He was alive." He sets the token down. "Whoever killed him left you with a complicated inheritance."

He is not sympathetic. He is calculating.

"What do you want from my office?"

choices.text: "A border pass. I need to continue the courier's route."
"Information. Who's been asking about the satchel?"
"I want to understand what happened to him."

sections.narrative:
You count out ten gold and set it on the desk.

The Captain regards it for a moment, then opens a locked drawer and produces a printed form. He fills it in with the speed of long practice, stamps it with three seals, and passes it across the desk.

"Legitimate Border Pass, valid for thirty days, standard merchant classification." He does not look at you as he says it. "The gate opens again in the morning. Arrive at the fourth hour."

The pass is real. It will pass any inspection in the second kingdom.

choices.text: Thank him and leave Varenmark at dawn

sections.narrative:
The Captain considers the five gold in your palm.

"That's half," he observes.

A pause. He is not offended; he is negotiating.

"Eight. That's my margin. I've got a clerk who asks questions about anomalies, and anomalies require paperwork, which requires people not to ask about the paperwork."

choices.text: Pay the eight gold
Counter-offer: five gold now, three more from the second kingdom
Decline and find another way

sections.narrative:
The Captain sits back and looks at you with the focused attention of someone revising their first impression.

"You're carrying something important," he says. Not a question. "And you need quiet passage. Those two things are usually separable from payment, in the right circumstances."

He lets that sit for a moment.

"Tell me about the courier."

choices.text: Tell him what happened on the road — honestly
Give him a version with the important facts omitted
Show him the Courier's Token

sections.narrative:
The Bribe Purse has weight to it. The Captain's eye moves to it with the automatic recognition of a man who has weighed many such purses.

"That covers the documentation fee and a portion of the administrative overhead," he says, which is the most diplomatic framing of accepting a bribe you have ever heard. He opens a form from his drawer.

"Name for the pass?"

choices.text: Give a false name and take the pass

sections.narrative:
The Captain looks at you for a long moment.

"Three parties," he says at last. "One sent a very polished man who asked questions at my gate about a royal courier passing through. Too polished for a soldier, too precise for a merchant. I had him watched. He spent two hours at the Ironbell Inn and left north this morning — which means he's ahead of you already."

He pauses to let that land.

"The second is a network I've seen operating in this city for three years. They use the back lanes. They are careful and they don't bother honest travellers. The third I know less about — recent arrivals, watching the road inns."

"Two of those three want what you're carrying. The third, I think, wants you to keep it."

choices.text: "What would it cost me to get through your gate?"
"The polished man — describe him for me."

sections.narrative:
The Captain studies you. Whatever he decides takes approximately four seconds.

"The courier corps has a warrant standing with my office. Any courier in the field can request an expedited pass under Section Twelve of the border protocols." He opens a drawer. "You are not a courier. But the man who held that token was, and if you're carrying his satchel north then someone somewhere needs you to succeed."

He fills out the form. Three stamps. He passes it across.

"Legitimate Border Pass. Don't lose it. And stay north of the second inn when you're in the second kingdom — there's a man there who's been asking about the southern road and he is not friendly."

choices.text: Thank the Captain and prepare to leave Varenmark at dawn

sections.narrative:
The Captain leans back and looks at the Courier's Token without touching it.

"A royal warrant issued under courier corps field authority," he says slowly. "That is what the token represents. And I would be within protocol to process a pass against it."

A pause.

"However. Couriers carry tokens and credentials both. The token establishes identity; credentials establish mission. You have one of those two things." He folds his hands. "I would be taking your word for the rest."

choices.text: "Then take my word."
"What would change the calculation?"

sections.narrative:
The man with the pipe looks at you with detached interest.

"You're looking for the lanes," he says. "The kind of lanes that help."

He speaks slowly, as if he has all the time in the world.

"Third alley past the fish stall. Door the colour of old blood. Knock twice, pause, twice again. Tell him the pipe-man sent you." He draws on the pipe. "He charges fair. He doesn't ask what the document is for."

choices.text: Go to the Forger's Workshop
Keep exploring the back lanes

sections.narrative:
The back road around Varenmark is local knowledge — a drover's track running east along the river bank, bypassing the gatehouse entirely and rejoining the Iron Road three kilometres north of the city. It is unpaved, slow, and watched by no official.

You ask a stablehand for directions and get a suspicious look and a grudging gesture. An hour later you are on the track, mud underfoot, hawthorn pressing close on both sides. No guards. No checkpoints.

Also no cover story if you are stopped north of the gate with no border pass in a kingdom that checks them.

choices.text: Continue on the back road and bypass the gatehouse entirely
Turn back — the risk isn't worth it without more preparation

sections.narrative:
Deeper into the back lanes, the buildings press closer. The light at midday barely reaches the ground.

You hear the two men before you see them — a scuff of boot on stone, too deliberate to be accidental. Then they step out of an alcove ahead: solid, unhurried, with the particular stillness of people who are comfortable waiting. They carry no uniforms. Their interest is specifically in you.

"The satchel," says the nearer one. No preamble. "Give it over and walk away."

His companion has moved to angle around you.

choices.text: Fight them both
Run back toward the market
"Who sent you?"

sections.narrative:
Two against one in a confined alley. You have the satchel in one hand, which is a liability, and the instinct of someone who has been running for two days, which is not nothing.

The first man is fast but not exceptional. You take a hit to the shoulder — nothing disabling — and put him against the wall hard enough that he stays there. The second hesitates a half-second too long. That is all you need.

The Spymaster gives a small, measured smile.

"A name is a liability in my profession," he says. "What I am is more useful than who: I run a network of — let us call them interested parties — across three kingdoms. We collect and move information. The kind of information that prevents certain kinds of conflict."

He turns his wine cup.

"What is in that satchel is the kind of information that could start one. I want to see it reach someone who can use it correctly. I believe you are, at this point, the best means of achieving that."

choices.text: "Why should I trust you?"
"What do you want from me specifically?"

sections.narrative:
"Trust is the wrong word," the Spymaster says. "We have aligned interests. I want the satchel delivered. You want to survive long enough to deliver it. The man who preceded you north this morning wants to intercept it. We are both served by your success."

He produces a sealed letter from his coat pocket and sets it on the table.

"This is a letter of introduction to my network contact in the second kingdom. It will open certain doors that are otherwise closed. Take it. Use it or don't — but having it costs you nothing and may save your life."

A pause. "The network can also give you a Forged Border Pass, or have a Spy Ring Cipher prepared if you want full access to the safe house network in the second kingdom. Both have costs. Tell me what you need."

choices.text: Accept the letter and also take a Forged Border Pass (3 gold)
Ask about the Spy Ring Cipher
Accept the letter only — find your own route to a pass

sections.narrative:
The contact produces a folded card from his coat — dense lines of encoded text, small and close, the cipher's logic visible in the repeated patterns if you know how to look.

"The Spy Ring Cipher identifies you to our network. Safe houses open to you, contacts recognise you, routes are shared. In the second kingdom, it will open the noble estate at Goldmere." He pauses. "It will also raise your visibility to anyone who knows what it means and is not on our side. A key and a liability simultaneously."

Alongside the cipher, he slides a completed border pass — merchant's classification, clean and convincing.

"Both available. Choose what serves you."

choices.text: Take both the Spy Ring Cipher and the Forged Border Pass (3 gold)
Take only the Spy Ring Cipher
Take only the Forged Border Pass (3 gold)
Take neither — find your own route

sections.narrative:
You pocket the Spy Ring Cipher. The contact gives a small nod of acknowledgement — not gratitude, exactly. Something more like professional recognition.

"The network's eyes will be on you in the second kingdom," he says. "Not watching over you. Watching — there is a difference. But if you need help, the cipher is how you ask for it."

He stands.

"You should leave Varenmark tonight or early morning. The man who moved north yesterday will have people at the second kingdom's road inns by midday tomorrow. Move faster than his network and you'll have a day's lead."

He is gone before you can respond to that. You have the cipher in your pocket, the satchel under your arm, and the Iron Road to the north. Varenmark has given you what it can. It is time to leave.

choices.text: Head to the customs gate and cross with your Forged Border Pass
You still need a border pass — return to find one

sections.narrative:
The customs gatehouse is bright with morning light. You present your Legitimate Border Pass to the clerk, who scans it with the practiced boredom of someone who has seen ten thousand of them. He stamps it without comment, hands it back, and waves you through.

The second guard at the outer arch gives the satchel a glance — couriers carry satchels; no one raises an eyebrow. The iron-bound gate swings wide.

Beyond it, the Iron Road opens onto a broad plain of pale grass. The frontier city of Varenmark is behind you. The second kingdom stretches ahead, flat and windswept and full of people who do not yet know you are coming.

You walk through without looking back.

choices.text: Press on up the Iron Road

sections.narrative:
The clerk at the customs gatehouse is a thin man with ink-stained fingers and a methodical air. He takes your Forged Border Pass, holds it up to the window, and rotates it slowly.

You keep your hands still. Your expression neutral. The satchel feels enormous under your arm.

The clerk sets the pass down and looks at you.

"Purpose of crossing?"

You answer. It comes out even, plausible. He writes something in his ledger. Then he looks at you again for a long moment before setting down his pen.

choices.text: Wait for the clerk's decision

sections.narrative:
The back road is a shepherd's track that hairpins through a shallow gulch before emerging in a stand of birch trees a kilometre north of the customs gate. You were directed to it by a contact who preferred not to be remembered.

The track is unused this morning. No guards. No checkpoints. The only witness is a crow on a fence post that watches you pass with professional indifference.

You emerge onto the Iron Road on the second kingdom side of the border and join the ordinary flow of traffic as if you have always been there. No stamp in any ledger. No record of your crossing.

No questions asked means no lies told. That is its own kind of freedom.

choices.text: Merge into the road traffic and head north

sections.narrative:
The Iron Road in the second kingdom is wider than you remembered, or perhaps Varenmark simply made everything feel narrow. Merchant caravans roll south with loaded wagons. Drovers move cattle in loose columns on the verge. A courier on horseback — royal livery, bronze token at the belt — passes at a canter without a glance.

You walk north. The satchel is slung close. The weight of it is familiar now, not comforting but present, like an old injury.

A day's walk ahead lies the Crossroads Inn, where the capital road branches off the main trade route. Every faction uses it. Everyone stops there. You cannot avoid it entirely — but you can choose how you arrive.

choices.text: Walk steadily north, staying in the traffic flow
Cut across the fields and approach the Crossroads Inn from the west

sections.narrative:
You fall in behind a merchant caravan — six wagons, a dozen guards, and twice that many workers. The caravan master is a broad woman who studies anyone who walks too close to her wagons and relaxes when they walk on. The road company is unremarkable and therefore perfect.

A military patrol rides past going south. Four soldiers, light cavalry kit. The lead rider's eyes sweep the caravan and move on. They are looking for quantity — smuggling volume — not individuals.

By late afternoon the Crossroads Inn is visible, its tiled roof rising above the poplars.

choices.text: Continue with the caravan to the inn
Break away before the inn and observe from the back lane

sections.narrative:
The field route is slower and wetter than you anticipated. The soil is loamy, recently ploughed, and your boots collect a significant share of the second kingdom before you reach the paved spur road that loops around to the inn's west gate.

The detour takes an extra hour but brings you in through the inn's stable yard, where the smell of horses and straw covers most things and the stable hands are too busy to wonder about muddy travellers.

You find a pump near the trough and clean your boots. The inn's rear entrance is ten steps away.

choices.text: Enter through the stable yard
Wait in the stable yard until dusk and watch who enters the inn

sections.narrative:
The clerk sets down the pass and calls over a senior guard.

They confer in low voices. The guard looks at you, looks at the satchel, looks at the pass again. Some feature of it — the watermark, the date, the seal impression — has aroused doubt even if it has not produced proof.

"We'll need your name in the register," the senior guard says. "And the contents of the satchel declared."

You give your name — a name — and you declare the satchel as correspondence. They write it down. They let you through. But you notice the junior guard dispatching a runner toward the city before you are ten steps past the gate.

Somebody now knows a face and a name, and they are moving faster than you are.

choices.text: Get moving before the runner reaches whoever they were sent to find

sections.narrative:
You find a quiet table at a roadside alehouse — not the Crossroads Inn, a timber-framed place where local farmers drink and no one cares about travellers.

The conversation around you is ordinary. Harvest prospects. A field boundary dispute. The price of salt.

But just before you leave, two men settle in at the corner table and speak in lower voices than their posture suggests they need to. You catch fragments.

"...the courier corps token... someone carrying it north..."

"...Lord's man at the Crossroads will be..."

Then one of them glances around and they drop lower still. You have heard enough. You leave before they notice you.

choices.text: Head directly to the Crossroads Inn

sections.narrative:
The Crossroads Inn is everything the road promises: large, busy, and neutral by reputation if not by practice. Three wings around a central courtyard, a stable yard to the east, a taproom that serves hot food until midnight, and rooms on the upper floor that cost more than they should.

You approach across the forecourt. A coach is being unloaded. Servants carry boxes. A factor in city clothes argues with a carter about weight limits.

Nobody looks at you. That could mean nothing, or it could mean everyone already knows where you are. You need to read this room carefully before anyone reads you.

choices.text: Enter the common room
Find the taproom and order a meal while you observe
Go directly to the innkeeper to arrange a room for the night

sections.narrative:
The common room is a long, low-ceilinged space with trestle tables and a fire that has been burning all day. Merchants, drovers, a pair of clerics, two soldiers off-duty in plain clothes. The ordinary human inventory of a busy road inn.

A man near the window catches your attention not by looking at you but by carefully not looking at you.

He is perhaps fifty, well-dressed in the manner of someone who travels frequently and has learned what roads do to fine cloth. He sits alone with a cup he is not drinking from and a ledger he is not reading.

Everything about him says merchant. Everything about him says something else.

choices.text: Take a seat across the room and watch him
Approach him directly

sections.narrative:
You get a drink, find a seat, and watch.

The man by the window is patient. He does not fidget. He has the stillness of someone accustomed to waiting — which means either a professional or someone very bored, and nothing about him suggests boredom.

After a quarter of an hour he glances at you. Not a searching look; a confirming one. As if you have just answered a question he already knew the answer to.

He closes his ledger, picks up his cup, and crosses the room toward you.

"You've been carrying that satchel since the ambush site," he says quietly, taking the seat opposite. "Closer to a week now. That's longer than most people last."

choices.text: "Who are you?"
Stand and prepare to leave immediately

sections.narrative:
"I represent the lord who ordered the courier's removal," he says, with no inflection on the word ordered, as if it were the most ordinary phrase in the world. "The satchel contains correspondence that embarrasses powerful people. Delivering it creates enemies you do not need and will not survive."

He sets the cup down.

"My employer will pay you twenty gold, your complete safety on the road, and a formal letter of clearance, in exchange for the satchel. No questions asked. No further contact. You walk away a wealthy person with a long life ahead."

He is unhurried. He is not threatening. He is describing a business transaction.

"You have until morning."

choices.text: "Twenty gold and a clearance letter. I'll think about it."
"I'll take your offer."
"No. The satchel isn't yours to buy."

sections.narrative:
He receives your refusal with a small nod, as if it confirms something he expected.

"That's a legitimate choice," he says. "Most people making legitimate choices don't reach the capital. The road between here and there has a great many possibilities."

He picks up his ledger.

"The offer will remain open until you're past the city gates. After that, it becomes something else entirely."

He leaves. You notice that no one in the common room watched him go — which means everyone was watching him go, carefully, in the way people watch things that frighten them.

choices.text: Remain at the inn for the night and decide your route in the morning
Leave the inn immediately — the Agent will not move tonight

sections.narrative:
He takes the satchel without ceremony. Twenty gold changes hands. The letter of clearance — stamped with a seal you do not recognise — joins your other papers.

He gives you a nod of something that is almost respect.

"You made the sensible choice. Travel safely."

He is gone before you can count the coins a second time. The satchel is gone. The weight of it — physical and otherwise — is simply absent.

You feel, simultaneously, lighter and hollow.

The Iron Road north is clear. The capital gates will pass you without incident. Whatever was in the satchel is no longer your problem, your purpose, or your burden.

choices.text: Continue north toward the capital

sections.narrative:
You tell him you need time to consider.

He accepts this with the equanimity of someone who was expecting it. He tells you the room at the end of the upper corridor is his until dawn. If you change your mind, knock twice.

He stands and moves toward the stairs without hurry.

You sit with your drink and your thoughts. The offer is clean, which is to say it is dishonest in a way you cannot see yet. Twenty gold is a large amount. Clear passage is larger. The fact that he is offering both means the satchel is worth considerably more than twenty gold to someone.

You are not selling the fate of three kingdoms for twenty gold. But first you need to know what you are holding.

choices.text: Sleep on it and decide in the morning
Knock on his door tonight and tell him no

sections.narrative:
Morning at the Crossroads Inn comes with the smell of bread and horses and the particular tension of a busy road establishment pretending to be calm.

You have slept, or tried to. The satchel was under your arm the whole night.

The man from last night is no longer in the common room. His table is empty. The innkeeper says he left before dawn — paid in advance, no forwarding word.

He is ahead of you on the road, or he has sent someone ahead. Either way, you are moving in the same direction as his network.

You need to decide: the main road, which is visible and watched, or a detour that costs time but loses pursuit.

choices.text: Take the main road north — speed matters more than stealth
Go to Goldmere Estate — the spy ring may have cover or information
Go to Goldmere Estate — the Spymaster's Letter may open the estate
Head to the Relay Station — the Courier's Contact may be there

sections.narrative:
The main road north of the Crossroads Inn is straight and well-maintained, flanked by drainage ditches and poplars that give no cover to anything larger than a crow.

You walk fast. The satchel is strapped tight. The Noble's Invitation — if you have it — sits in your jacket beside papers you no longer need.

The road is busy enough that pursuit would be obvious: anyone following would have to maintain a gap or close in, and there is nowhere to do either without being seen. By midday you have covered twelve kilometres without incident. The land is rising. Somewhere ahead, behind a ridge, the road bends east toward the capital's outer approaches.

choices.text: Keep the pace — reach the Capital Approach before dark
Stop at a roadside shrine and check if you are being followed

sections.narrative:
The track to Goldmere Estate branches east from the main road at a marker stone carved with a stylised G. A courier on foot would not normally be heading this way — but you are not a courier anymore, if you ever were.

The estate track is well-kept, lined with chestnut trees dropping early leaf. The estate itself comes into view after twenty minutes: a stone house, not quite a manor, with a walled kitchen garden and outbuildings that speak of working wealth rather than decorative wealth.

At the gate, a young servant asks your name. You give it. He goes inside. A minute later he returns and opens the gate without a word.

choices.text: Enter Goldmere Estate

sections.narrative:
The Noble Host meets you in the estate's formal sitting room — a room used for practical discussions dressed up as formal ones.

He is a man of perhaps sixty, lean and dry-voiced, with the measured movements of someone who has been careful all his adult life. He does not ask about the satchel directly. He asks about the road from Varenmark, about the Crossroads Inn, about the man you may or may not have spoken with there.

"He'll be at the capital gates before you," the Noble Host says. "His people are faster on horseback and slower to make mistakes than most of the others."

He refills your cup.

"The spy ring can help you. Whether that's what you want is a question only you can answer."

choices.text: "What can the spy ring offer me?"
"I need to keep moving. What's the fastest route?"

sections.narrative:
"A route into the palace district that doesn't go through the main gates," the Noble Host says. "A contact inside the Spymaster's network who can carry a message ahead. And a piece of information about the satchel's contents that the assassins' employer very much does not want you to have."

He slides a sealed card across the table. Not to be opened here, he explains. It confirms what the satchel is carrying: evidence of a treaty negotiation that was supposed to be secret, involving parties who have publicly denied it. If that evidence reaches the right hands in the palace, someone loses everything.

He produces the Noble's Invitation — a formal card on thick paper.

"This gets you past road checkpoints with a credible cover. Take it."

choices.text: Accept the Noble's Invitation and take your leave

sections.narrative:
The Noble Host walks you to the estate gate personally.

"There's a spy ring courier leaving this estate at dusk," he says. "He goes fast and knows the back ways. If you want a message carried to the palace district ahead of you — to the Spymaster's contact there — I can arrange it now."

He is offering you a hand you do not fully understand. That is not, in itself, a reason to refuse it.

choices.text: Send a message ahead with the spy ring courier
Decline — the fewer people who know your route the better

sections.narrative:
You leave Goldmere Estate as the afternoon light lengthens. The chestnut trees cast long shadows across the track.

The main road is ten minutes west. Once you rejoin it, the Capital Approach is perhaps half a day's walking.

You are carrying more information now than when you arrived at the estate. That is both useful and dangerous. The Noble Host knows you were here. That knowledge will spread, as all knowledge spreads, faster than you travel.

But you have the Noble's Invitation in your pocket — if you took it — and the road ahead is open.

choices.text: Rejoin the main road and continue north

sections.narrative:
The Relay Station sits back from the Iron Road behind a low stone wall, its gate marked by a royal courier corps flag — blue with a bronze torch, slightly faded. A proper fortified waystation: two storeys, shuttered arrow slits on the upper floor, a stable that smells recently used.

The sentry at the gate is a young woman in courier corps uniform. She is not hostile, but she is thorough.

"Your purpose?"

You explain. She asks for documentation.

choices.text: Present the Courier's Token
Claim you have an urgent message for the station warden

sections.narrative:
The sentry examines the token with the focused attention of someone who knows exactly what she is looking at. She straightens.

"I'll fetch the warden."

The warden arrives inside three minutes: a compact man in his forties, silver-haired, with the posture of someone who has been in the corps for twenty years and expects twenty more. He studies the token. He studies you.

"How did you come by this?"

You tell him the version of the truth that is most useful. His bearing changes, as if a variable he had been holding as unknown is now resolved.

choices.text: Tell him everything — the courier, the ambush, the satchel
Tell him only that you are carrying a courier's delivery for the capital

sections.narrative:
The warden listens without interrupting. He has the quality of a man who processes information before responding to it.

When you finish he asks two questions. The first is procedural and you answer it cleanly. The second is whether you know what is in the satchel.

You answer that too, honestly or not, and watch him nod.

"There is someone here you should speak to," he says. "Whether they are still here is another matter."

He leads you inside without further elaboration.

choices.text: Follow the warden inside

sections.narrative:
The warden leads you to a side room off the station's main corridor — a room set up for long occupation: a cot, a desk with papers, a cold meal tray.

An old man sits in the chair by the window. He is past seventy, wrapped in a traveller's coat despite the warmth of the room, with eyes that are alert in a face that is exhausted.

The Courier's Contact.

"You made it," he says. Not surprised. Relieved in the way of someone who has been calculating odds. "Sit down. Tell me what happened to Marden."

Marden. The courier. You finally have a name for the dead man on the Iron Road.

choices.text: Tell him about the ambush and what you have carried since

sections.narrative:
He listens to everything. He asks nothing while you speak. When you finish, he is quiet for a moment.

"The satchel contains evidence of a secret treaty between the northern lords and a foreign power," he says at last. "Marden was carrying it to the palace. If it reaches the royal archivist, the treaty is void and the lords who signed it face charges of treason. That is why they sent a kill team."

He looks at the satchel.

"I cannot take it here. The station is not secure enough — they know where I am. You need to carry it to the palace anteroom. Ask for the royal archivist by name — it's on the satchel's exterior seal."

He produces the Relay Station Key and holds it out.

"This gets you in through the east postern of the palace district. Do not come in through the main gate — the Lord's Agent will have watchers there."

choices.text: Take the key and go — the capital is half a day away

sections.narrative:
The side room is empty.

The cot has been slept in recently. The papers on the desk are gone — not filed, swept. One sheet is on the floor: encoded, meaningless to you, but it has a dark smear at the corner that might be dried mud and might be something worse.

The warden says nothing for a moment.

"He was here yesterday evening," he says finally. "There was a disturbance in the night. I assumed..."

He does not finish. He does not need to. The Courier's Contact is either dead, taken, or fled. The assassins moved faster than either of you expected.

choices.text: "Can you tell me anything about what he was carrying?"
Leave immediately — linger here and you share his fate

sections.narrative:
The warden tells you what he knows, which is less than you hoped: the Contact was carrying orders to the palace archivist, the satchel Marden had been delivering was expected, and at least two of the Lord's people knew about this relay station.

He also gives you something the Contact left behind intentionally — a note, sealed, addressed to the royal archivist by name.

"He said to give it to whoever came for the satchel if he couldn't deliver it himself," the warden says. "I hope that's you and not whoever killed him."

The note gives you a name and a room number in the palace district. You have a destination, even without a living guide.

choices.text: Thank the warden and move toward the capital

sections.narrative:
You stop at a roadside wayshrine — a small stone alcove with a faded relief of a road deity and a good view in both directions.

You wait and watch for ten minutes.

There is ordinary traffic. There is one figure, perhaps half a kilometre back, who stops when you stop and starts again when you start. It might be coincidence. The road is long; people walk at similar speeds.

It might not be coincidence. The road is long; professionals know how to maintain a gap.

You pick up your pace. Whoever they are, you are not stopping to find out today.

scripts.onEnter: if state.get('refusedLordsAgent') or state.get('stalledLordsAgent') then ctx.showMessage('The Lord\'s Agent will not let you walk away without a final answer.') end

choices.text: Press on toward the Capital Approach at speed

sections.narrative:
The land rises. The poplars give way to quarried stone walls that rise on either side of the road as it enters the cutting leading to the capital's outer approaches. The road narrows from its full width to something more constrained.

You can see the capital from here: a smudge of towers and smoke above the next ridge, impossibly near after the distance you have come.

A checkpoint is visible ahead. A gatehouse across the road, two guards visible.

choices.text: Approach the checkpoint directly
Look for a way around the checkpoint

sections.narrative:
The checkpoint guards check papers for everyone, not selectively. That is either good news or bad news depending on what your papers say.

One of the guards holds out a hand for your documents. You hand them over. He reads them. He looks at you.

choices.text: Wait while he considers

sections.narrative:
The guard takes your papers, examines them for approximately three seconds, and hands them back.

"Purpose in the capital?"

You answer. He nods. The gate swings open.

It is, perhaps, the easiest moment of the last week. You walk through a checkpoint without incident for the first time since the ambush, and the simplicity of it is almost disorienting.

The Capital Approach lies ahead.

choices.text: Continue to the Capital Approach

sections.narrative:
The guard takes your papers and takes his time with them. He passes them to his colleague, who also takes his time.

"Sealed satchel," the first guard says. "Courier's designation?"

You answer. He makes a note. The second guard is looking at your face in a way that suggests he is comparing it to a description he has been given.

"Wait here."

He goes inside the gatehouse. You stand in the road. Thirty seconds. A minute. The sun is very bright on the pale stone.

choices.text: Wait — bolting now would confirm their suspicions
Offer a Bribe Purse to smooth things over
Present the Noble's Invitation as cover

sections.narrative:
The guard returns. He hands back your papers.

"We had a report of a courier corps token being carried by an unauthorised individual. You don't match the description."

He is lying, or he was told to say that, or he was genuinely satisfied. You cannot tell which. It does not matter. The gate opens.

"Safe journey."

You walk through. The checkpoint is behind you. Somewhere in the gatehouse, a note is being written or not written, a message sent or not. The Lord's Agent's network is faster than paperwork.

For now, you are through.

scripts.onEnter: if ctx.hasItem('Bribe Purse') then ctx.removeItem('Bribe Purse'); state.set('suspicion', math.max(0, state.get('suspicion') - 1)) end

choices.text: Continue to the Capital Approach

sections.narrative:
There is a drainage cut on the east side of the road, following the base of the quarried wall. It is barely wide enough for a person carrying a satchel, but barely wide enough is enough.

You move along it quickly, keeping low. The checkpoint guards are talking to a carter; their attention is forward and west. The drainage cut takes you past the gatehouse wall and deposits you in a weedy verge on the far side.

You straighten up, join the road traffic, and keep walking as if you have always been on this side of the checkpoint.

choices.text: Continue quickly toward the Capital Approach

sections.narrative:
Two figures step out of the shadow of the quarry wall.

They are not the Lord's Agent — but they work for him. You can tell by the way they position themselves: one in front, one at a diagonal. Not amateurs. They have done this before.

"No need for this to be complicated," the nearer one says. "The satchel. That's all."

They are blocking the road. The wall is on your left. The drainage cut is behind you.

choices.text: Fight — you did not come this far to be stopped here
Run back toward the checkpoint — let the guards sort it out
Throw something to distract them and run

sections.narrative:
The fight is short and violent and goes better than it has any right to.

The first one rushes. You use the satchel's weight as a counterweight and the stone wall as leverage and he hits the road harder than he intended. The second one pulls a knife.

You use what you have — the blade if you carry it, your elbows and momentum otherwise. The second man decides that whatever he is being paid is not quite enough for this particular afternoon.

He runs. The first is groaning on the road behind you.

You are bleeding from something minor, shaking from something significant, and moving again before the dust settles.

choices.text: Keep moving — the capital gates are close

sections.narrative:
The Capital Approach.

The Iron Road makes its final turn and there it is: the city walls, the towers, the gate traffic of the capital in afternoon light. Hundreds of people moving in and out. Smoke from ten thousand chimneys. The noise of a city that does not stop.

You have walked the length of the Iron Road. From the ambush site to the forest to the border city to the second kingdom to here. The satchel is with you — or its business is finished — but either way you have arrived.

The last stage of the road stretches before you. Whatever happens next happens in the capital.

choices.text: Enter the capital

sections.narrative:
You stand at the threshold of the capital.

The gate road is busy. Merchants, travellers, officials, servants. The noise and press of a city that is the end of the Iron Road and the beginning of everything else. Inside those walls are the factions that have been moving against each other since before you picked up the satchel. Inside are the answers to the questions you have been carrying.

You check the satchel one last time — or note its absence. You take stock of what you carry: in your hands, in your pockets, in the choices you have made since the ambush site.

Then you step through the gate.

choices.text: Enter the capital and find your way to the palace district

sections.narrative:
The city gates rise ahead of you — two towers of dressed stone flanking an iron-banded arch wide enough for three coaches abreast. Guards in the capital livery stand at each side, checking papers and waving most travellers through. Most.

You join the queue. Your pulse is steady or it is not, but either way you keep your face composed. The Sealed Satchel — if you still carry it — is hidden beneath your coat. The city presses close: hawkers, porters, a sergeant shouting at a stopped cart.

As you near the front of the queue you take stock of how you look to these guards. How many eyes have marked you since the ambush on the Iron Road?

scripts.onEnter: local s = state.get('suspicion'); if s >= 10 then ctx.navigateTo(134) elseif s >= 5 then ctx.navigateTo(133) else ctx.navigateTo(132) end

sections.narrative:
The guard glances at you, nods, and waves you through without asking for papers. You are just another traveller arriving on the last of the afternoon light. The gate arch passes over your head and you are inside the capital.

The city opens up like a held breath releasing — wide cobbled streets, the smell of smoke and baking bread, the distant beat of a crier's drum. Nobody is watching you. Not yet.

choices.text: Head toward the market district
Bear left toward the docks approach
Head directly for the palace district

sections.narrative:
The guard at the head of the queue holds up a hand. He is a broad-shouldered man with a sergeant's stripe and the look of someone who has been told to watch for a particular type of traveller today.

"Papers," he says. It is not a question.

Behind him, half-listening, is a man in a plain coat who does not belong to the guard detail. He is watching the queue with a professional stillness that you recognise. The Capital Gate Captain steps forward to join the sergeant.

"Lot of travel from the east this week," the Captain says pleasantly. "Anyone with business at the palace needs a countersigned pass. Do you have one?"

choices.text: Show your Courier's Token
Show your Relay Station Key
Show your Noble's Invitation
Offer a bribe
Claim to be a merchant with business in the market

sections.narrative:
The queue has barely moved before a hand closes on your arm. Not a guard — something worse. A plain-coated man stepping out of a doorway alcove as you pass. He speaks quietly, close to your ear.

"Don't shout. Don't run. You've been seen since Varenmark."

There are two of them — the man beside you and another blocking the path ahead. Behind you the queue has closed off. People are deliberately not looking.

This has the feel of something that has been prepared.

choices.text: Break left and run into the crowd
Reach for your Assassin's Blade
Go with them — it may be a faction contact, not an arrest
Shout for the guards

sections.narrative:
The Captain's eyes go to your hand, to the purse, and back to your face. He makes a small gesture and the sergeant takes a step back, suddenly interested in the traffic on the other side of the road.

"I think your papers are in order," the Captain says. "Welcome to the capital."

The coin vanishes. You walk through the gate.

choices.text: Head toward the market district
Bear left toward the docks approach
Head directly for the palace district

sections.narrative:
You push into the crowd at the gate — a press of bodies, cursing porters, a cartload of feed grain blocking the arch. For a moment you are just one more body moving against the flow. You hear a shout behind you, and then the crowd swallows the sound.

You come out on a side lane that runs parallel to the gate road. Your heart is loud in your chest. No one is following — not yet. But you are inside the city now, and they know your face.

choices.text: Get clear — head toward the market district
Go to the docks and think

sections.narrative:
It is the wrong instinct. The moment your voice rises the plain-coated men produce sealed warrants. The guards respond to the warrants, not to you. You are taken to a gatehouse room and someone with no official title asks you questions for a long time.

You answer some of them. Not enough.

Three days later a notice appears on the city board: an unnamed courier, convicted of carrying seditious material and consorting with known enemies of the Crown. The satchel is opened in a magistrate's chamber. What was inside it does not survive the trial.

Neither do you.

The market district spreads across the capital's central quarter — a roofed arcade of stalls giving way to open squares, then to covered halls thick with cloth merchants, spice traders, and the kind of booth that sells nothing visible but always has a man in the back room.

You know the Spymaster is here. Their letter — if you carry it — named this district, a covered stall near the south arcade. You have also heard that the Lord's Agent has a presence here, working through a factor who operates from the textile quarter.

The crowds are both cover and exposure. You move carefully.

choices.text: Seek out the Spymaster's contact in the south arcade
Look for the Lord's Agent's factor in the textile quarter
Pass through the market and head for the palace district
Double back and head for the docks

sections.narrative:
The south arcade is where the capital's lesser merchants sell medicines, dyes, and curiousities. You find the stall described in the Spymaster's letter — or, if you do not carry the letter, a stall whose owner matches the description you were given in Varenmark: a heavyset woman selling pressed herbs, whose eyes count you the moment you arrive.

"The herb seller's rate is ten a bundle," she says without looking up. "Unless you're asking about something that isn't herbs."

She means the Spymaster. She can bring you to them — or she can tell you they are not available today.

scripts.onChoices: if ctx.hasItem('Spymaster\'s Letter') then ctx.addChoice('Show the letter — prove you have a prior arrangement', 140) end

choices.text: Ask to meet the Spymaster directly
This feels like a trap — walk away

sections.narrative:
The Spymaster receives you in a room above the arcade that smells of cedar and old paper. They are not what you expected — quieter, older, with the patient manner of someone who has been doing this long enough that urgency has left them entirely.

They look at the satchel — or its absence — for a long moment.

"You've come further than I thought you would," they say. "Most people in your position are dead by Varenmark. The offer still stands. Give me the satchel and I will see you out of the capital tonight with a new name and enough coin to begin somewhere else."

Then, if you carry the Spymaster's Letter: "The letter reduces the price. I respect that you kept it intact."

Their price, with or without the letter, is the same thing: the satchel. Nothing else will do.
